# load libraries
```{r}
library(randomForest)
library(DALEX)
library(ggplot2)
library(xgboost)
library(rio)
library(caret)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(Matrix)
library(Metrics)

```


# import inbuilt data

```{r}
data(mtcars)

mtcars$am <- factor(mtcars$am,
                    levels = c(0, 1),
                    labels = c("Automatic", "Manual"))

df <- mtcars[, c("am", "mpg", "hp", "wt", "cyl")]

head(df)
```


# train random forest model
```{r}
set.seed(42)
rf_model<- randomForest(
  am~.,
  data=df,
  ntree=100,
  importance=TRUE
  
)
print(rf_model)
```




# create a DAlex explianer

- the explainer will act as  a bridge btn the machine learning model and xai tools
```{r}
y_num<-ifelse(df$am =="Manual", 1,0)
explainer<-DALEX::explain(
  model=rf_model,
  data=df[, -1],
  y=y_num,
  label="Random Forest",
  verbose=FALSE
)
```


# global excplainability? feature importance
## which model influence the model the most?
- Dalex measures feature importance by shuffling variables and observing how much model perform
```{r}
 global_importance<-model_parts(
   explainer,
   type= "variable_importance"
 )
global_importance
```


# plot global importance
```{r}

plot(global_importance)+
  ggtitle("GLOBAL FEATURE IMPORTANCE")+
  theme_minimal()
```
### interpretation
- the lager the more important the variable is

# set  a native Random fOrest Importance
```{r}

importance(rf_model)

```

# convert into a bar chart
```{r}
importance_df<-data.frame(
  Variable= rownames(importance(rf_model)),
  Importance=importance(rf_model)[,"MeanDecreaseGini"]
)
importance_df<-importance_df[
  order(importance_df$Importance,
  decreasing=TRUE),
]
```

# plotting
```{r}
ggplot(
  importance_df,
  aes(
    x=reorder(Variable, Importance),
    y=Importance
  )
)+
  geom_bar(stat="identity")+
  coord_flip()+
  labs(
    title="Random Forest Variable Importance ",
    x="variable",
    y="mean Decrease Gini"
  )+
  theme_classic()

```



#  select car
```{r}
new_car<-df[1, -1]
new_car
```

# make prediction
```{r}
predict(
  rf_model, new_car
)
```

# actual class
```{r}
df$am[1]
```


# generate local explanation
- breakdown explanation show how each variable contribute to global to a single prediction
```{r}
local_explanation<- predict_parts(
  explainer, 
  new_observation= new_car,
  type= "break_down"
)
print(local_explanation)
```
# plot local explanation
```{r}
plot(local_explanation)+
  ggtitle(
     "why did the model predict manual transmission")
```
